name: Seneca Falls Convention
kicker: First U.S. women’s rights convention · Launched the fight for the vote
briefing: In July 1848, about 300 people crowded into a small chapel in upstate New York for the first women’s rights convention in the United States. Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott led it, and Stanton’s Declaration of Sentiments boldly declared that “all men and women are created equal.” Its demand that women get the right to vote was so controversial that it was the only resolution that did not pass unanimously, but it launched a 72-year fight that ended with the 19th Amendment in 1920.
answerHtml: Seneca Falls Convention (accept Seneca Falls Women’s Rights Convention; prompt on women’s rights convention)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Charlotte Woodward, a young glove maker who signed this event’s most famous document, was the only signer known to have lived to see the 19th Amendment ratified in 1920. That document was signed by 68 women and 32 men.
tossups.r: Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott organized this 1848 meeting. For 10 points, name this first women’s rights convention, held in upstate New York.

tossups.p: James Mott, a Philadelphia merchant, chaired the second day of this event, when the general public was invited to attend. Many of the people at this event were Quakers or abolitionists, and James’s wife was one of its two main organizers.
tossups.r: She was Lucretia Mott, and the other was Elizabeth Cady Stanton. For 10 points, name this first U.S. women’s rights convention, held in 1848.

tossups.p: This event was planned over tea at the home of Jane Hunt in Waterloo, New York, by five women, including Mary Ann M’Clintock and Martha Coffin Wright. Wright’s sister, a well-known Quaker minister, helped lead it.
tossups.r: That minister was Lucretia Mott. For 10 points, name this 1848 women’s rights convention, also organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton.

tossups.p: At this event, the ninth resolution, which said it was the duty of women to secure their “sacred right to the elective franchise,” was the only resolution that did not pass unanimously. Frederick Douglass spoke in favor of that resolution.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1848 convention in New York that launched the American women’s suffrage movement.

tossups.p: A document read at this event complained that man had made a married woman “civilly dead” in the eye of the law and had taken from her even the wages she earned. Its very first complaint was that women had never been allowed to vote.
tossups.r: That document, the Declaration of Sentiments, was modeled on the Declaration of Independence. For 10 points, name this 1848 women’s rights meeting.

tossups.p: Two of this event’s organizers met in London in 1840, when women who came as delegates to the World Anti-Slavery Convention were made to sit apart and were not allowed to take part. Eight years later, those two women planned this meeting in New York.
tossups.r: They were Lucretia Mott and Elizabeth Cady Stanton. For 10 points, name this first women’s rights convention in the United States.

tossups.p: Days after this event, Frederick Douglass praised it in his Rochester newspaper, _The North Star_. At this event, Douglass had argued that women deserved the vote just as much as men, helping one controversial resolution pass.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1848 convention led by Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott.

tossups.p: About 300 people, including dozens of men, gathered at the Wesleyan Chapel, a Methodist church that welcomed antislavery speakers, for this two-day event. Most of its organizers were Quakers who were also active in the fight against slavery.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this first women’s rights convention, organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott.

tossups.p: Some of the 100 people who signed this event’s main document later removed their names after newspapers mocked the meeting. Frederick Douglass, the famous abolitionist editor, was one of the 32 men who signed and kept his name on it.
tossups.r: That document said “all men and women are created equal.” For 10 points, name this 1848 meeting led by Elizabeth Cady Stanton.

tossups.p: Two weeks after this event, many of its supporters held another women’s rights convention in Rochester, New York, and this time a woman, Abigail Bush, was chosen to preside. This event, by contrast, had been chaired by a man on its second day.
tossups.r: The first one was organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott. For 10 points, name this first women’s rights convention in the United States.

tossups.p: In 1980, Congress created the Women’s Rights National Historical Park to preserve the chapel where this event took place, along with the nearby home of one of its organizers. The town where it met is also home to the National Women’s Hall of Fame.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1848 convention led by Lucretia Mott and Elizabeth Cady Stanton.

tossups.p: A Quaker minister who helped lead this event worried that its demand for voting rights would make the meeting look ridiculous, but her co-organizer insisted on including it. That co-organizer wrote most of the event’s main document.
tossups.r: Those women were Lucretia Mott and Elizabeth Cady Stanton. For 10 points, name this 1848 women’s rights convention.

tossups.p: Three years after this event, Amelia Bloomer introduced its main organizer to a temperance activist in the same town, beginning a partnership that lasted about 50 years. That newcomer, Susan B. Anthony, had not attended this event.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1848 women’s rights convention in upstate New York, organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton.

tossups.p: On this event’s 75th anniversary in 1923, Alice Paul announced her proposed Equal Rights Amendment at a gathering in the same town and named it for one of this event’s organizers, a Quaker minister from Philadelphia.
tossups.r: That organizer was Lucretia Mott. For 10 points, name this 1848 meeting where Elizabeth Cady Stanton presented the Declaration of Sentiments.

tossups.p: A newspaper notice announced that this event would discuss “the social, civil, and religious condition and rights of woman” on a Wednesday and Thursday in July. The notice said the first day would be for women only.
tossups.r: Lucretia Mott was among the advertised speakers. For 10 points, name this 1848 meeting in upstate New York, the first women’s rights convention in America.

trap.title: Where was Susan B. Anthony?
trap.body: Susan B. Anthony is the most famous suffragist, so players often assume she was at Seneca Falls, but she did not attend; she met Elizabeth Cady Stanton three years later, in 1851. Players also mix up this 1848 meeting with its own document, the Declaration of Sentiments, and with later meetings such as Worcester (1850), the first national women’s rights convention, and Akron (1851), where Sojourner Truth spoke.
trap.fix: If the question asks for “this meeting” or “this convention,” say Seneca Falls; if it asks for “this document,” say the Declaration of Sentiments. Seneca Falls clues: 1848, Stanton and Lucretia Mott, the Wesleyan Chapel, 68 women and 32 men, and Frederick Douglass.
trap.line: Real answer line: Seneca Falls Convention (prompt on women’s rights convention)
